octopus.your_low_carbon_score_is_based: Your Low Carbon Score is based on National Energy System Operator’s (NESO) annual forecast for carbon density. As of 2025, they deem the anything below 99gCO₂/kWh as low, and therefore greener.

performance.used_for_clipping_left_at_4: Used for clipping. Left at 4.3, Fox Plant uses the rating in your inverter’s model name (EVO 10-5-H → 5 kW).
performance.worked_out_from_each_array_s: Worked out from each array’s panel datasheet values and mounting (Device → PV Configuration), its output, and the outdoor temperature and wind from your weather sensors.
pv.postcode_area_hint: The first part of your postcode, for anything that needs your region, such as the regional carbon forecast. Only that part is stored or sent.
pv.auto_calculated_from_installation_dat: Auto-calculated from installation date {installDateStr} ({ageLabel} · {months} months) at {rate}% loss per year.
pv.autohint_what_is_the_efficiency_facto: {autoHint} What is the efficiency factor?
pv.installation_date_installdate_from_so: Installation date {installDate} (from Solcast settings) — efficiency is calculated automatically and saved daily on each install-date anniversary (00:15 local).
pv.nameplate_nameplatekw_kw_dc_effective: Nameplate {nameplateKw} kW DC · Effective {effectiveKw} kW (after efficiency)
pv.nominal_operating_cell_temperature_fr: Nominal Operating Cell Temperature from the panel datasheet (often 42–47 °C).
pv.on_the_roof_a_few_cm: On the roof, a few cm above the tiles
pv.open_rack_ground_mount_free_air: Open rack / ground mount (free air behind)
pv.panel_angle_from_horizontal_default_2: Panel angle from horizontal (default 25° if unset)
pv.panel_count_wattage_efficiency_tilt_a: Panel count, wattage, efficiency, tilt, and azimuth drive the native Solcast rooftop PV forecast on Overview and Energy charts.
pv.panels_with_less_air_behind_them: Panels with less air behind them run hotter in the same sun.
pv.set_an_installation_date_under_settin: Set an installation date under Settings → Solcast to auto-calculate efficiency from system age.
pv.solcast_style_performance_loss_per_ye: Solcast-style performance loss per year (default 2% — pro-rated by month since installation).
pv.temperature_coefficient_of_pmax_on_th: “Temperature coefficient of Pmax” on the datasheet, e.g. −0.30.
pv.what_is_the_efficiency_factor: What is the efficiency factor?
quick_settings.all_soc_limits_must_be_at: All SOC limits must be at least {soc_min_pct}%.
quick_settings.could_not_load_battery_so: Could not load battery SOC history. Enable the Home Assistant recorder for battery_soc.
quick_settings.day_to_day_inverter_contr: Day-to-day inverter controls — battery SOC limits, work mode, baseline charge windows, and plant control.
quick_settings.enter_a_whole_number_perc: Enter a whole-number percentage for each SOC limit.
quick_settings.export_floor_exp_must_be_: Export floor ({exp}%) must be ≤ system max ({max}%).
quick_settings.force_export_stops_at_the: Force-export stops at the purple handle; Self Use resumes below it
quick_settings.fox_plant_owns_the_schedu: Fox Plant owns the schedule on Home Assistant. Each segment sets work mode, SOC limits, and optional force-charge via Remote Control for its time window — applied every minute when that window is active. The timetable is not stored on the inverter (unlike the Fox app).
quick_settings.implements_energy_managem: Implements energy management strategies by setting battery SOC and import limits according to production schedules, reducing overall energy consumption during peak periods.
quick_settings.inverter_is_under_externa: Inverter is under external remote control (read-only status on EVO).
quick_settings.map_battery_soc_in_foxess: Map battery SOC in FoxESS Modbus, then reload FoxESS Plant.
quick_settings.minimum_for_all_three_lim: Minimum for all three limits is 10%. Keep off-grid min ≤ system min ≤ system max. On the EVO, system max can't be below Max SOC From Grid: lowering system max lowers it too, and raising system max raises it back if they were equal.
quick_settings.no_battery_soc_history_fo: No battery SOC history for today yet.
quick_settings.no_custom_schedules_yet_a: No custom schedules yet — add one to match the Fox app “Add a Schedule” screen.
quick_settings.no_soc_history_for_socid_: No SOC history for {socId}. Enable the Recorder for battery_soc (5-minute statistics or state history).
quick_settings.off_grid_min_min_must_be: Off-grid min ({min}%) must be ≤ system min ({mid}%).
quick_settings.off_grid_system_min_max_w: Off-grid / system min / max write to the inverter. Export floor is virtual (SmartCharge only) — force-export stops there and returns to Self Use so you keep house battery.
quick_settings.optimised_for_self_consum: Optimised for self consumption, reduce reliance on grid electricity.
quick_settings.ordinary_inverter_strateg: Ordinary inverter strategy — force charge/discharge is separate on EVO.
quick_settings.period_max_is_written_to_: Period max is written to the inverter’s system max SOC while this segment runs.
quick_settings.prefix_saved_on_ha_segmen: {prefix}saved on HA — segment not active now; applies at window start
quick_settings.prioritises_electricity_s: Prioritises electricity sales to generate income.
quick_settings.quick_controls_for_your_p: Quick controls for your plant. Drag the three handles — off-grid min, system min, system max
quick_settings.remote_control_active_rc_: Remote control active: {rc} (use FoxESS Modbus Remote Control to change; not a work mode).
quick_settings.soc_limits_work_mode_and_: SOC limits, work mode, and charge windows are managed by SmartCharge while automation is on.
quick_settings.stored_in_the_inverter_s_: Stored in the inverter’s schedule slot. With force charge on, the inverter charges until Max SOC, then holds it until the slot ends.
quick_settings.system_max_max_cannot_be_: System max ({max}%) cannot be below the current battery level ({live}%). Discharge or wait for SOC to drop.
quick_settings.system_min_mid_must_be_ex: System min ({mid}%) must be ≤ export floor ({exp}%).
quick_settings.system_min_mid_must_be_sy: System min ({mid}%) must be ≤ system max ({max}%).
quick_settings.tailored_for_areas_with_u: Tailored for areas with unstable power grids. Reserves SOC to prevent power outages.
quick_settings.the_schedule_is_stored_on: The schedule is stored on the inverter (its own Mode Scheduler), so it keeps running even if Home Assistant is offline. Fox Plant checks it regularly and re-writes it if it was changed elsewhere — don't edit the schedule in the Fox app while Fox Plant is in control. Up to 6 slots; a slot crossing midnight uses two. Force-charge slots stop at their max SOC and charge at SmartCharge’s max charge rate.
quick_settings.used_for_any_time_not_cov: Used for any time not covered by a custom segment (Fox app “Remaining Time Mode”).
quick_settings.when_active_fox_plant_is_: When active, Fox Plant is the only writer for charge periods (via foxess_modbus). Release control if you need to edit schedules in the Fox app temporarily.
quick_settings.work_mode_entity_not_foun: Work mode entity not found. Reload the integration.
reports.could_not_load_energy_report_ena: Could not load energy report. Enable the Home Assistant recorder and keep history for energy sensors.
reports.map_power_entities_in_foxess_mod: Map power entities in FoxESS Modbus, then reload FoxESS Plant.
reports.no_detail_rows_for_this_period: No detail rows for this period.
reports.no_power_history_for_today_yet: No power history for today yet.
reports.no_statistics_for_listed_confirm: No statistics for: {listed}. Confirm the Recorder stores 5-minute means for these entities (same as your Lovelace plotly-graph card).
reports.open_analysis_or_wait_for_histor: Open Analysis or wait for history to load.
reports.statistics_chart_unavailable_rel: Statistics chart unavailable. Reload the panel or refresh the page.

sc_day.no_data: Nothing to show for this day yet.
sc_day.no_plan_recorded: No SmartCharge plan was recorded for this day, so only what the battery did is shown.
sc_day.planned_soc_not_recorded: The planned battery level wasn’t recorded for this day (Fox Plant keeps it from 0.9.541 on), so the Plan row shows the planned charge and export times only.
settings.configure_your_plant_automation: Configure your plant, automations, and integrations
settings.create_a_key_in_the_foxess: Create a key in the FoxESS Cloud Open API portal (API management).
settings.foxess_open_api_used_only_for: FoxESS Open API, used only for battery warmup (a cloud-only setting). Inverter control and scheduling use Modbus.
settings.foxess_open_api_used_only_to: FoxESS Open API, used only to change battery warmup settings (the inverter shows them over Modbus but won’t accept changes that way). settings.foxess_plant_found_reloading_pa: FoxESS Plant found — reloading panel registration…
settings.home_assistant_entity_picker_is: Home Assistant entity picker is not available
settings.leave_blank_to_auto_discover_fo: Leave blank to auto-discover FoxESS entities from your installation.
settings.leave_blank_to_use_the_pcs: Leave blank to use the PCS serial from Modbus. Fox Cloud scheduler calls need the inverter deviceSN from your Fox account — if test fails with error 41200, open the Fox portal device list and paste that SN here.
settings.loading_entities_if_this_stays_: Loading entities… If this stays empty, reload FoxESS Plant and ensure weather warning binary sensors exist in Home Assistant.
settings.managed_by_smartcharge_detail_o: Managed by SmartCharge{detail} Open SmartCharge to change SOC limits, charge windows, and work mode while automation is on.
settings.no_google_weather_alerts_match_: No Google Weather alerts match. Install Google Weather with alerts enabled, or show all sensors.
settings.no_identity_entities_discovered: No identity entities discovered yet. Update foxess_modbus, reload Home Assistant, then reload this panel.
settings.no_matches_for_triggerfilter_tr: No matches for “{triggerFilter}”. Try “alert”, “warning”, or show all sensors.
settings.set_by_your_installer_on_the: Set by your installer on the inverter; not shown in the Fox app. Read-only.
smart_charge.a_charge_or_export_is_only: A grid charge or battery export is only planned if it saves at least this much per kWh moved, so tiny savings don’t add battery cycles.
smart_charge.carbon_source_regional: the regional carbon intensity forecast for {postcode}
smart_charge.carbon_source_national: the national carbon intensity forecast (Great Britain)
smart_charge.carbon_status_failed: Carbon Forecast: couldn’t be loaded ({error}), so this does nothing until it loads. Tried again every hour.
smart_charge.carbon_status_pending: Carbon Forecast: loads when you save, from the national carbon intensity service (free, no account).
smart_charge.allow_forced_export_in_safe: Allow Battery Export in Max Safety
smart_charge.building_plan_from_tariff_r: Building plan from tariff rates, Solcast forecast and house load history…
smart_charge.charge_export_windows_smart: Charge/export windows SmartCharge planned — the kWh is predicted. “Used” shows whether the battery actually charged (or exported) in that window.
smart_charge.charge_windows_come_from_th: SmartCharge picks the charge times itself from your rates, so there’s no timetable to set. When a planned charge starts, the inverter is told to charge from the grid with Max SOC set to the planned level, so it stops once that’s reached.
smart_charge.charge_windows_set_on_the_i: Charge windows set on the inverter — not necessarily importing right now.
smart_charge.could_not_load_smartcharge_: Could not load SmartCharge analysis. Enable the recorder for smart charge and power sensors.
smart_charge.daily_savings_from_solar_an: Daily savings from solar and battery
smart_charge.double_check_live_meter_imp: Before a grid charge starts, compare the import rate your meter reports with your supplier’s rate. If they differ by more than the Rate Tolerance, the charge is held and checked again.
smart_charge.e_g_api_0_037p_and: How far apart two rates can be and still count as the same: at 0.5p, 24.50p and 24.85p agree. The Octopus rate re-check during a charge uses it too.
smart_charge.enable_smartcharge_in_devic: Enable SmartCharge in Device → SmartCharge to use this report.
smart_charge.export_is_a_fixed_export_ma: Export is a fixed {export_max_p}. SmartCharge only force-exports when that beats refilling the battery later from cheaper import.
smart_charge.export_pays_at_most_export_: Export pays at most {export_max_p}. Only {effText} of a stored kWh comes back out, so that’s never more than refilling it at your cheapest import ({import_min_p}): force-exporting the battery can’t save money, so SmartCharge never does it on these rates. Surplus solar still exports as normal.
smart_charge.flat_average_load_used_unti: A flat house load used until there’s load history to predict from.
smart_charge.forces_a_fresh_octopus_fetc: At this time each day SmartCharge fetches fresh rates and rebuilds the plan (Agile publishes tomorrow’s rates around 16:00). Half-hours without a published price are estimated but never scheduled.
smart_charge.forces_a_fresh_rate_fetch_a: At this time each day SmartCharge fetches fresh rates and rebuilds the plan.
smart_charge.forecast_pv_is_divided_by_t: Max Safety divides the solar forecast by this: 1.25 plans on 80% of the forecast. The other modes use the forecast as it is.
smart_charge.full_length_slot_charge_and: Full {length}-slot charge and export plan from {start} to {end}
smart_charge.half_hourly_house_load_is_p: SmartCharge predicts each half-hour’s house load from this many days of the inverter’s load history, with recent days counting more, and weekdays and weekends kept separate once there’s enough history.
smart_charge.import_is_a_flat_import_max: Import is a flat {import_max_p}p/kWh, so grid charging can’t save money. SmartCharge will just run self-use unless prices change.
smart_charge.in_operating_mode_no_price_: in {operating_mode} — no price saving to make
smart_charge.load_from_fallback_kw_no_hi: load from fallback kW (no history yet)
smart_charge.lowest_cost_charge_cheap_ex: Lowest bill: charges at the cheapest times and exports the battery when it pays.
smart_charge.max_discharge_hint: The most the battery can supply in the plan, for the house and for exports. Blank = same as Grid Charge Power. On an EVO, planned exports run at the inverter’s full rating.
smart_charge.max_profit_is_value_on_your: Max Profit is {value} on your tariff: import is a flat price and exporting stored energy can’t beat refilling it, so there’s nothing extra to earn. Max Safety fits better.
smart_charge.meter_check_not_on_agile: Not used on Agile or Tracker: the meter isn't sent the half-hourly prices, so its rate isn't the real price (Fox Plant re-checks the Octopus API every 5 minutes while charging instead).
smart_charge.min_export_price_hint: Battery export is only planned in half-hours that pay at least this.
smart_charge.no_armed_smartcharge_sessio: No armed SmartCharge sessions recorded in this period.
smart_charge.no_daily_plan_slots_in_reco: No daily plan slots in recorder history for this period.
smart_charge.no_daily_smartcharge_activi: No daily SmartCharge activity for this period.
smart_charge.no_export_tariff_found_so_s: No export tariff found, so SmartCharge won’t force-export the battery. Surplus solar still exports as normal.
smart_charge.no_hems_audit_events_logged: No HEMS audit events logged for this period yet. Events are recorded when SmartCharge rebuilds its daily plan, arms export, detects a plunge price, or pairs spread slots.
smart_charge.no_smartcharge_plan_history: No SmartCharge plan history recorded for this period yet.
smart_charge.not_used_smartcharge_uses_y: Not used: SmartCharge uses your battery’s measured efficiency, {value}% (lifetime battery discharge ÷ charge, which includes inverter and standby losses).
smart_charge.outage_reserve_hint: SmartCharge keeps enough in the battery to run the house for a while if the grid goes down: house load × Outage Hours × Outage Safety Margin (× the Outage Reserve Multiplier in Max Safety). It plans so the battery doesn’t fall below this, or the inverter’s Min SOC if that’s higher. Planning only: the inverter’s own Min SOC isn’t changed.
smart_charge.planned_planned_charge_kwh_: Planned {planned_charge_kwh} grid charge — skipped, solar forecast covered it
smart_charge.plans_on_pessimistic_solar_: Plans on less solar and more house load than forecast, and keeps a bigger outage reserve.
smart_charge.plunge_api_said: API said {value}p/kWh inc VAT · first seen {seen} · confirmed {count}×
smart_charge.plunge_evidence_hint: Every half-hour Octopus's API showed as negative, and every half-hour SmartCharge charged from the grid in: the exact rate the API returned (with the request URL, when it was fetched and Octopus's own server time), any later change to it, what Fox Plant did, and the grid import across the half-hour from your smart meter (via Glow) and the inverter. The meter's own price isn't recorded: on Agile the meter isn't sent the half-hourly prices, so that rate isn't the real price. While charging from the grid, Fox Plant asks Octopus again every 5 minutes; if the API contradicts the price the plan used, SmartCharge re-plans on Octopus's rate (which stops a charge that isn't worth it) and that's recorded too. Download it to send to Octopus if your bill doesn't match.
smart_charge.plunge_none_yet: No negative-price half-hours recorded yet. They're recorded from the Octopus API as soon as it shows one.
smart_charge.put_each_planned_grid_charg: On: each planned grid charge is written to the inverter as a Force Charge slot 30 minutes before it starts, and each planned export as a 20-minute Force Discharge slot that Fox Plant keeps extending. The inverter starts and stops them itself, so a charge carries on even if Home Assistant goes down, and an export stops within 20 minutes. Off: Fox Plant holds Remote Control on for the whole charge or export.
smart_charge.ran_on_solar_battery_no_gri: Ran on solar + battery — no grid action needed
smart_charge.recheck_hint: How long a held charge waits before the rate is checked again.
smart_charge.requires_fox_plant_control_: Needs Fox Plant in control, your tariff’s rates and a solar forecast (Solcast or Open-Meteo).
smart_charge.outage_load_hint: House load to assume during an outage. Blank = your predicted average load.
smart_charge.safety_reserve_multiplier_h: Max Safety only: multiplies the outage reserve (see Outage Reserve & House Load), so 1.5 keeps 50% more. Max Profit uses 1.0.
smart_charge.saved_is_smartcharge_s_own_: “Saved” is SmartCharge’s own estimate of what its scheduling added vs plain self-use. The “System saved” headline is the whole solar + battery system vs buying everything from the grid.
smart_charge.share_of_the_battery_above_: How much of the battery between the Export Floor and Max SOC may be exported each day: 1 = all of it, 0.35 = about a third. Starts again at midnight.
smart_charge.simulates_the_battery_half_: Simulates the battery half-hour by half-hour from your tariff, the Solcast PV forecast and your house-load history, then picks the cheapest charge and export slots. Keeps an outage reserve floor. StormSafe always overrides.
smart_charge.smartcharge_always_also_wak: How often SmartCharge re-checks rates, forecast and battery and updates the plan. It also runs at every half-hour so planned charges start on time. On Octopus Tracker it checks at most hourly.
smart_charge.smartcharge_fox_home_batter: SmartCharge: Fox home battery charging from solar and off-peak grid
smart_charge.smartcharge_may_empty_the_b: Lets SmartCharge discharge the battery to the grid (Force Discharge) when the export price is worth more than refilling the battery later. Surplus solar exports as normal either way.
smart_charge.time_of_use_tariffs_the_gri: Time-of-use tariffs only. The battery is planned to still hold this much when the most expensive band ends, as spare for loads the forecast can’t predict (an oven, a kettle). If the battery is heading below it before the next cheap band, a top-up at a dearer rate may be planned. Set it to your inverter’s Min SOC plus the biggest surprise load you want covered. Planning only: the inverter’s own Min SOC isn’t changed.
smart_charge.tomorrow_s_pv_estimated_fro: tomorrow's PV estimated from the same time yesterday until the next poll
smart_charge.use_your_live_glow_hildebra: Your Glow or IHD import unit-rate sensor (£/kWh or p/kWh). Leave blank to skip the check.
smart_charge.used_by_smartcharge_overrid: Used by SmartCharge (overrides Quick Settings while automation is active). StormSafe can still charge above the system max when armed. The purple Export floor is virtual — SmartCharge stops force-export there and returns to Self Use.
smart_charge.used_to_size_how_many_half: The power the inverter is told to charge at during a planned grid charge, and what SmartCharge uses to work out how long each charge takes. Keep it within what your inverter and battery can take.
smart_charge.used_until_the_inverter_has: How much of each kWh put into the battery comes back out (0.9 = 90%). Used until Fox Plant can measure it from the inverter’s battery totals (after 50 kWh charged).
smart_charge.value_the_plan_always_runs_: {value} The plan always covers up to the end of tomorrow, and is also rebuilt when rates, the solar forecast or the battery SOC change noticeably, and at least hourly.
smart_charge.outage_hours_hint: How many hours the reserve should cover. 0 = no outage reserve.
smart_charge.zero_export_negative_price_: While the export price is below 0p, set the inverter's Export Power Limit to 0 W. The inverter stays in Self Use: solar still runs the house and charges the battery, it just doesn't feed the grid. The limit you had is saved and put back when the price goes positive (also after a restart, when this is turned off, or on Release Control). Needs an inverter with a writable Export Power Limit.
smart_charge.prefer_greener_charging_hin: When charging costs the same in several half-hours, pick the ones where the grid is running on more wind and solar. It never charges more or pays more for it, so on a time-of-use tariff it usually changes nothing. Uses your regional carbon forecast if a postcode area is set in PV Configuration, otherwise the national one.
smart_charge.zero_export_status_idle: Export Limit: Not Changed · export price isn't negative
smart_charge.zero_export_status_no_contr: Export Limit: This Inverter Has No Writable Export Power Limit
solar_forecast.all_figures_in_kwh_error_: All figures in kWh. Error is how far each model's forecast, made a day ahead, was from what your panels actually produced, on average over the last 30 days. The blend gives more weight to the more accurate models; until a model has {value} scored days the models share equally.
solar_forecast.automatic_update_of_forec: Automatic update of forecasts from sunrise to sunset
solar_forecast.average_difference_betwee: Average difference between the forecast made a day ahead and what the panels produced, over the last 30 days
solar_forecast.check_foxess_plant_is_loa: Check FoxESS Plant is loaded, then refresh the page.
solar_forecast.daily_greener_night_snaps: Daily greener-night snapshots will build here ({value} stored).
solar_forecast.daylight_schedule_hours_h: Daylight schedule: {hours} h between sunrise and 1 h before sunset · about {interval} min between refreshes (spread across your {api_limit}/day API limit) · polls until {until} · {inWin}
solar_forecast.diagnostic_sensors_expose: Diagnostic sensors expose detailed_forecast for automations — charts use plant state directly.
solar_forecast.each_refresh_uses_1_reque: Each refresh uses 1 request per unique tilt/azimuth group. In daylight mode, your {api_limit} daily calls are spread from sunrise until 1 hour before sunset (from Home Assistant sun.sun).
solar_forecast.enable_pv_strings_in_pv_c: Enable PV strings in PV Configuration to request rooftop forecasts.
solar_forecast.estimate_from_a_previous_: Estimate from a previous day (no forecast reaches tomorrow)
solar_forecast.every_solcast_request_goe: Every Solcast request goes through one place in Fox Plant, which records it here (last 30). Automatic requests are at least 10 minutes apart and stop for a day after a whole day of refusals.
solar_forecast.forecasts_compared_with_m: Forecasts compared with measured solar output
solar_forecast.hobbyist_accounts_may_reg: Hobbyist accounts may register two rooftop sites on Solcast → Locations. Enter the latitude and longitude exactly as shown there for the site you use. Do not copy Home Assistant home coordinates — extra decimal places will not match Solcast and API calls can fail or return the wrong site.
solar_forecast.hobbyist_plans_are_typica: Hobbyist plans are typically 10/day — used to spread automatic polling.
solar_forecast.installation_date_cannot_: Installation date cannot be in the future.
solar_forecast.installation_date_must_be: Installation date must be YYYY-MM-DD (match your Solcast Home PV system listing).
solar_forecast.latitude_and_longitude_ar: Latitude and longitude are required. Copy them exactly from one of your two registered Solcast hobbyist locations (not Home Assistant coordinates).
solar_forecast.latitude_must_be_between_: Latitude must be between -90 and 90; longitude between -180 and 180.
solar_forecast.linking_to_solcast_home_p: Linking to Solcast Home PV site(s)… save settings
solar_forecast.measured_production_vs_so: Measured production vs Solcast and Open-Meteo forecasts, with Solcast's intraday revisions
solar_forecast.no_forecast_comparison_da: No forecast comparison data for this day yet.
solar_forecast.no_solcast_requests_recor: No Solcast requests recorded yet. Every request Fox Plant makes is listed here.
solar_forecast.outside_window_before_sun: outside window (before sunrise or within 1h of sunset)
solar_forecast.paused_after_a_day_of_ref: Paused after a day of refusals · next try {when}
solar_forecast.pick_at_least_one_open_me: Pick at least one Open-Meteo weather model.
solar_forecast.pv_generation_vs_forecast: PV generation vs forecast power and cloud cover
solar_forecast.quota_resets_resetwhen_ne: Quota resets {resetWhen} · next poll at sunrise ({sunriseWhen})
solar_forecast.refusals_since_download.o: {count} refusal since the last successful download{value2}.
{count} refusals since the last successful download{value2}.
solar_forecast.register_a_free_home_pv_s: Register a free Home PV System account (10 API requests/day). All quota goes to PV forecasts — no weather calls.
solar_forecast.replaces_a_third_party_so: Replaces a third-party Solcast integration for chart PV lines
solar_forecast.same_field_as_solcast_add: Same field as Solcast Add Home PV System (used for age derating on their site). Optional here — not sent to the rooftop API yet. Use your best estimate if unsure.
solar_forecast.saved_as_solcast_coord_de: Saved as {solcast_coord_decimals} decimal places to match typical Solcast listings. Saved site: {coordDisplay}{value}
solar_forecast.smartcharge_sizes_the_ove: SmartCharge sizes the overnight grid charge from tomorrow's solar forecast. Use Solcast, Open-Meteo or both: Fox Plant compares them with what your panels actually produce and switches to Open-Meteo by itself when Solcast stops updating. Overview weather and StormSafe stay on Google Weather.
solar_forecast.solcast_hobbyist_api_free: Solcast hobbyist API (free account, 10 requests a day).
solar_forecast.solcast_hobbyist_api_ok_l: Solcast hobbyist API OK (listed Home PV sites)
solar_forecast.test_connection_lists_you: Test connection lists your Home PV systems (does not use daily forecast quota).
solar_forecast.test_lists_your_home_pv_s: Test lists your Home PV systems from the Solcast toolkit (does not use your daily forecast quota).
solar_forecast.turn_on_solcast_or_open_m: Turn on Solcast or Open-Meteo below.
solar_forecast.used_for_each_enabled_pv_: Used for each enabled PV string by Solcast and Open-Meteo. Panel count, wattage, and efficiency are under Settings → PV Configuration. Saved together when you press Save below.
solar_forecast.uses_hobbyist_rooftop_sit: Uses hobbyist rooftop_sites/{resource_id}/forecasts (matched to your toolkit Home PV sites)
solar_forecast.value_daily_snapshots_sto: {value} daily snapshots stored. Dates ever flagged greener stay recorded even if Octopus later changes the forecast.
solar_forecast.x_24_h_mode_about_value_m: 24 h mode: about {value} min between refreshes.
storm_safe.arm_storm_pre_charge_when_goo: Arm storm pre-charge when Google hourly forecast shows severe weather within the lead time
storm_safe.arms_when_google_weather_repo: Arms when Google Weather reports a storm-type condition (or alert binaries turn on)
storm_safe.categories_unavailable.one: {count} category is unavailable for {title} — Google does not publish those alerts or forecast types there.
storm_safe.categories_unavailable.other: {count} categories are unavailable for {title} — Google does not publish those alerts or forecast types there.
storm_safe.choose_which_google_weather_c: Choose which Google Weather conditions trigger StormSafe pre-charge.
storm_safe.conservative_factor_on_solcas: Conservative factor on Solcast PV (default 1.35 — higher = less trust in forecast). SmartCharge uses 1.15; StormSafe uses a larger margin because backup matters more than cost.
storm_safe.direct_inverter_control_while: Direct inverter control while StormSafe is armed — not a timed charge schedule. Solcast may turn off grid import when PV covers the gap.
storm_safe.enable_the_option_below_to_ev: Enable the option below to evaluate whether solar can cover the battery gap before grid import.
storm_safe.forecast_labels_in_hours_h_go: Forecast: {labels} in ~{hours}h (Google hourly: {token}) — pre-charge active. Uncheck that category below to stop.
storm_safe.if_battery_is_below_this_leve: If battery is below this level when a forecast storm is due, grid pre-charge is used even when Solcast looks sufficient (default 90%).
storm_safe.important_when_storm_conditio: Important: When storm conditions are active now, or battery SOC is below your safety floor, full grid pre-charge always applies regardless of this setting. Turning this option off always uses grid pre-charge when StormSafe arms.
storm_safe.no_storm_triggers_active_righ: No storm triggers active right now.
storm_safe.off_by_default_enable_only_if: Off by default — enable only if you accept relying on forecast solar before severe weather
storm_safe.only_needed_if_you_are_not: Only needed if you are not using Google Weather alerts, or you want extra sensors (MeteoAlarm, NWS, templates).
storm_safe.optional_when_a_storm_is_only: Optional. When a storm is only in the forecast (not active yet), Fox Plant can compare your battery gap to Solcast solar expected before the storm hour. If PV covers the gap (with a safety margin), StormSafe arms without grid import — saving import cost while still monitoring the weather.
storm_safe.pre_charge_before_severe_weat: Pre-charge before severe weather — Google Weather detects storms; optional Solcast can reduce grid import when forecast solar covers the gap
storm_safe.press_save_stormsafe_settings: Press Save StormSafe settings to apply option changes and refresh this calculation.
storm_safe.pv_likely_sufficient_grid_imp: PV likely sufficient — grid import can be skipped
storm_safe.pv_top_up_only_no_grid: PV top-up only — no grid import
storm_safe.select_a_google_weather_locat: Select a Google Weather location above to see which Fox-style warning categories Google publishes for your area.
storm_safe.solcast_is_not_set_up_yet: Solcast is not set up yet — add your API key under Settings → Solcast and configure PV strings before turning this on.
storm_safe.storm_prep_is_active_pv_top: Storm prep is active — PV top-up only (no grid import per Solcast pre-check).
storm_safe.storm_prep_is_active_storm_pr: Storm prep is active — storm pre-charge applied.
storm_safe.stormsafe_home_battery_backup: StormSafe: home battery backup during a storm
storm_safe.target_max_leave_empty_to_kee: Target max % (leave empty to keep current max)
storm_safe.toggle_the_severe_weather_typ: Toggle the severe weather types that should trigger StormSafe for {title}. Each row shows which Google hourly forecast tokens map to that category (e.g. rainy → Heavy rain). Uncheck a category to ignore that forecast. Grey rows are not offered by Google Weather in this region.
tariff.a_sensor_that_reports_your_export: A sensor that reports your export price (its upcoming rates too, if it lists them).
tariff.a_sensor_that_reports_your_import: A sensor that reports your import price — or an Octopus Energy integration rate sensor, whose upcoming rates SmartCharge also plans with.
tariff.apply_band_work_mode_to_inverter: Apply band work mode to inverter
tariff.choose_a_sensor_that_reports_this: Choose a sensor that reports this rate
tariff.connect_your_energyproviderlabel_: Connect your {energyProviderLabel} account below: import rates and hour bands sync automatically.
tariff.connected_export_tariff_value_val: Connected — export tariff {value}, {value2} rates. Press Save Export to use it.
tariff.daily_standing_charge_in_currency: Daily standing charge in {currency} — published to the plugin sensor on save
tariff.electricity_rates_for_cost_and_re: Electricity rates for cost and revenue analysis. Import and export can each come from a supplier, a Home Assistant sensor, or rates you type in — the same supplier for both, or different ones.
tariff.export_from_a_different_supplier_: Export from a different supplier than import: sign in to {energyProviderLabel} here. Only its export meter is used.
tariff.export_rates_come_from_the_export: Export rates come from the export meter on your {energyProviderLabel} account.
tariff.export_saved_but_the_fetch_failed: Export saved, but the fetch failed: {err}
tariff.from_your_octopus_dashboard_devel: From your Octopus dashboard (Developer settings → API access).
tariff.import_rates_and_hour_bands_are: Import rates and hour bands are synced from {supplierLabel} automatically whenever rates are fetched. Export is Manual Rates: type each band's export rate below and Save Tariff — it is kept on every sync. Work Mode and Force Charge per band can still be configured.
tariff.live_state_state_value_could_not: Live state: {state}{value} — could not convert to {currency} automatically
tariff.no_export_supply_on_this_fuse: No export supply on this Fuse account
tariff.not_configured_add_rates_for_cost: Not configured — add rates for cost analysis
tariff.not_configured_yet_save_at_least: Not configured yet — save at least one rate above.
tariff.not_saved_yet_press_save_export: Not saved yet — press Save Export.
tariff.on_a_computer_sign_in_at: On a computer, sign in at eonnext.com,
tariff.plugin_sensor_pluginentityid_upda: Plugin sensor: {pluginEntityId} — updated on schedule boundaries for recorder history
tariff.plugin_sensors_are_created_when_y: Plugin sensors are created when you save. They update at each hour boundary so the recorder captures when costs change (same path planned for Agile API tariffs).
tariff.plugin_sensors_value_rates_update: Plugin sensors: {value} — rates update at each hour boundary so the recorder captures when costs change.
tariff.press_f12_console_paste_it_and: , press F12 → Console, paste it and press Enter, then paste the token here.
tariff.quick_settings_mode_scheduler_is_: Quick Settings mode scheduler is enabled — it takes priority over tariff band work modes.
tariff.rates_and_hour_bands_are_synced: Rates and hour bands are synced from {supplierLabel} automatically whenever rates are fetched (including the 30-minute poll). Work Mode and Force Charge per band can still be configured below.
tariff.rates_are_stored_in_the_selected: Rates are stored in the selected currency. Changing currency does not convert existing values — re-enter rates after switching.
tariff.save_to_create_plugin_sensors_tha: Save to create plugin sensors that update each hour (or when the band changes)
tariff.search_by_friendly_name_or_entity: Search by friendly name or entity id.
tariff.search_by_sensor_name_or_entity: Search by sensor name or entity id (e.g. sensor.octopus_energy_electricity_meter_rate).
tariff.set_by_from_change_it_on: Set by {from} — change it on the Export card
tariff.smartcharge_is_currently_active_p: SmartCharge is currently active — per-band Work Mode and Force Charge are not applied while it is enabled.
tariff.synced_from_energyproviderlabel_a: Synced from {energyProviderLabel} automatically whenever rates are fetched — published to the plugin sensor in {currency}/day
tariff.tariff_configured_ready_for_cost_: Tariff configured — ready for cost analysis.
tariff.type_export_rates_per_band_in: Type export rates per band in the Daily Time-of-Use Schedule above — e.g. a fixed SEG rate.
tariff.type_import_rates_per_band_in: Type import rates per band in the Daily Time-of-Use Schedule above.
tariff.use_the_home_assistant_sensor_pic: Use the Home Assistant sensor picker — search by friendly name or entity id.
tariff.waiting_for_a_numeric_reading_fro: Waiting for a numeric reading from the selected sensor
tariff.when_enabled_each_hour_applies_th: When enabled, each hour applies that band’s work mode (and optional force charge) while plant control is on.
tariff.x_24_hourly_blocks_from_00_00: 24 hourly blocks from 00:00 to 24:00, same every day. Pick a band colour, then tap hours to assign it. Use one band for a flat tariff, or two to four for peak/off-peak.
warmup.battery_warmup_keeping_the_home_b: Battery WarmUp: keeping the home battery warm on a winter night
warmup.battery_warmup_not_reachable_via_:
Battery warmup not reachable via Fox Cloud API
{value} Open the Fox portal device list and confirm the inverter deviceSN under Settings → Fox API — it is often different from the Modbus PCS serial ({value2}).
warmup.battery_warmup_refreshed_from_fox: Battery warmup refreshed from Fox Cloud
warmup.during_these_windows_grid_power_i: During these windows, grid power is allowed to warm the battery (up to three slots, like the Fox app).
warmup.enable_the_fox_cloud_api_under: Enable the Fox Cloud API under Settings → Fox API and save your API key first. Warmup is controlled via Fox Cloud (not Modbus).
warmup.fox_returned_an_error_when_readin: Fox returned an error when reading batteryHeating settings.
warmup.grid_assisted_battery_heating_dur: Grid-assisted battery heating during low-price periods. Settings sync with your inverter via Fox Cloud.
warmup.heats_the_battery_when_it_falls: Heats the battery when it falls below {start_temperature}°C, up to {end_temperature}°C{value}.
warmup.heats_the_pack_in_cold_weather: Heats the pack in cold weather, using grid power in the low-price slots below
warmup.pre_heat_the_battery_pack_in: Pre-heat the battery pack in cold weather using grid power during cheap-rate windows — matches the Fox app Battery warmup screen.
warmup.saved_waiting_for_the_inverter_to: Saved. Waiting for the inverter to confirm via Fox Cloud (usually a minute or two).
warmup.tip_fox_app_as_the_battery: Tip (Fox app): as the battery SOC is <40%, only PV and grid energy (if enabled) will be used. Battery energy will not be used for self-warming.
warmup.warmup_is_off_the_battery_won: Warmup is off: the battery won't be heated, however cold it gets.
warmup.warmup_starts_when_the_battery_fa: Warmup starts when the battery falls below this ({start_min}–{start_max}°C).
warmup.warmup_stops_once_the_pack_reache: Warmup stops once the pack reaches this ({end_min}–{end_max}°C).
warmup.your_import_price_is_the_same: Your import price is the same all day, so there’s no cheaper window to pick.
weather.add_google_weather_to_show_an: Add Google Weather to show an hourly forecast.
weather.choose_your_google_weather_locat: Choose your Google Weather location. StormSafe uses official alert binaries (if available) and/or the weather condition sensor.
weather.each_home_assistant_config_entry: Each Home Assistant config entry is one place Google tracks (usually your home). StormSafe reads current weather and forecast from the entry you choose.
weather.enable_the_weather_condition_sen: Enable the Weather condition sensor in HA if hidden (eye icon).
weather.filled_sensor_mappings.one: Filled {count} sensor mapping from local station
weather.filled_sensor_mappings.other: Filled {count} sensor mappings from local station
weather.forecast_no_storm_in_the_next: Forecast: no storm in the next {value} hours.
weather.hacs_custom_repositories_ha_goog: HACS → Custom repositories → ha_google_weather
weather.looking_for_ecowitt_gw2000a_wh90: Looking for Ecowitt / GW2000A / WH90-style sensors. If nothing is detected, use the entity search on each row.
weather.map_local_pws_ecowitt_sensors_fo: Map local PWS / Ecowitt sensors for Performance
weather.map_local_weather_station_sensor: Map local weather station sensors for Performance microclimate (wind cooling, rain, dew). Forecast weather from StormSafe / Google remains available as a fallback.
weather.native_google_weather_current_co: Native Google Weather — current conditions + hourly forecast. Pre-charges when a storm is due within your lead time (below).
weather.no_automatic_match_search_home_a: No automatic match — search Home Assistant entities below.
weather.no_google_weather_config_entries: No Google Weather config entries found. Add the integration under Settings → Devices & services.
weather.no_weather_condition_sensor_foun: No weather condition sensor found for this integration entry. Update Google Weather or pick another source under Advanced.
weather.not_found_on_typical_ecowitt_sta: Not found on typical Ecowitt stations.
weather.optional_ambient_air_temp_ecowit: Optional ambient air temp. Ecowitt: Outdoor Temperature.
weather.optional_outdoor_humidity_ecowit: Optional outdoor humidity. Ecowitt: Humidity (not Indoor).
weather.optional_weather_used_when_a_map: Optional weather.* used when a mapped sensor is blank. Defaults to StormSafe / Google Weather.
weather.outdoor_dewpoint_ecowitt_dewpoin: Outdoor dewpoint. Ecowitt: Dewpoint (not Indoor Dewpoint).
weather.primary_cooling_microclimate_sig: Primary cooling / microclimate signal. Ecowitt: Wind Speed.
weather.return_here_enable_stormsafe_pic: Return here, enable StormSafe, pick your Google Weather location, and press Save StormSafe settings
weather.select_a_location_below_then_pre: Select a location below, then press Save StormSafe settings.
weather.settings_integrations_add_google: Settings → Integrations → Add → Google Weather (API key + your home location)
weather.use_rain_rate_not_daily_weekly: Use rain rate (not daily/weekly totals). Ecowitt: Rain Rate Piezo.
weather.usually_not_on_ecowitt_leave_bla: Usually not on Ecowitt — leave blank or map another sensor if you have one.
weather.weather_data_source_for_stormsaf: Weather data source for StormSafe — live conditions, hourly forecast lead time, and optional severe-weather alert sensors from the Google Weather integration in Home Assistant.
